transcript:
Header: 2026-05-21 09:30 PDT | Duration: 1h15m | Attendees: Priya, Marcus, Sofia, Evan, Ana, Daniel

Summary (auto): Align on rollout safety net and define bakeoff + soak plan. Assign owners and timelines.
Link references: https://redwood.internal/docs/rollout-safety-net (draft), https://redwood.internal/s/reports/bakeoff-template

[00:00:00] Priya: okay, uh, let's kick off — thanks everyone for making time. main goal today is to lock the safety-net steps for the rollout and agree the bakeoff plan so we can be confident on perf and cost before we open traffic.

[00:00:27] Marcus: yeah, quick callout — SRE is worried about warm-up patterns, basically tail latency hitting at minute 2 during sudden spikes. we should be explicit about cache warming, kv cache, like K V cash — the transcription on last run was weird — and session pinning.

[00:00:49] Sofia: agreed. also want to make sure VPC peering and cross-region egress for EU is validated; we had a mis-route with a test last month where traffic went out via the wrong nat gateway and added 40ms.

[00:01:12] Evan: for the bakeoff, my proposal: two axes. first axis quantization profile: q8 (8-bit) vs q4 (4-bit / 4-bit nf4). second axis kernel variant: new fused-attn kernel vs fallback kernels. run the same workload through both and measure p50/p95/p99, cost per 1k tokens, and quality regression on a small eval set.

[00:01:41] Ana: and QA will add smoke prompts for hallucination/regression checks — we'll do a qualitative pass with our canary prompt set. it includes safety triggers, hallucination probes, and structured output checks.

[00:02:05] Daniel: operationally, i want a dry-run scheduled where release engs push the canary across 2 AZs, then we ramp traffic 1% -> 5% -> 20% over 6 hours if metrics look good. Failures at any step should auto-fall back to the prior model variant.

[00:02:27] Priya: sounds good. let's enumerate acceptance criteria. what are the hard gates? p99 latency under 450ms for gen-xx workloads? or is 500ms acceptable at 20%?

[00:02:44] Marcus: i'd say p99 under 500ms on canary at 20% with steady-state load and no invocation errors >0.5%. error budget check must be green. also no increase in token cost over baseline more than 15% without explicit signoff.

[00:03:06] Evan: to add, quality must not degrade beyond our threshold on the prompt set — we use a combined metric: automated BLEU-ish score + human spot checks. if the auto metric drops >2.5% we hold. that number is negotiable but we need a limit.

[00:03:29] Ana: and we'll run a small human review batch for the top 200 responses in the canary window. that gives us a human signal for new failure modes.

[00:03:45] Sofia: infra needs: pre-baked nodes with kernel 3.14 and fallback image available. also ensure automatic node replacement and drained pods use the warm-cold cache lifecycle. once a node is replaced we should re-warm kv cache for 15 minutes before accepting full traffic.

[00:04:08] Priya: ok, so bakeoff plan details — Evan, can you outline the exact steps?

[00:04:14] Evan: sure. step 1: run synthetic throughput sweep on both quant profiles to get deterministic throughput curve. step 2: run e2e workload (mixed short + long sequences) for 8 hours to look for memory growth/kv-cache leak. step 3: run quality eval on 2k prompts, auto metric + sample human review. step 4: 72h soak at target throughput with periodic bursts to simulate real traffic. logs shipped to /s/reports/bakeoff-run-<date>.

[00:04:45] Marcus: for the soak, include scheduled GC windows, network flaps simulation, and kube eviction events. we need to validate graceful degradation and fallback to cheaper model variant if eviction rate passes threshold.

[00:05:04] Priya: what thresholds do we use for auto-fallback?

[00:05:08] Marcus: if pod ready percentage drops below 95% or CPU at 95% for >5 minutes, trigger fallback. also if OOM rates increase by >0.1% over baseline during soak, that's a failure.

[00:05:30] Daniel: can release engs implement a circuit-breaker that switches routing by policy? i.e., if latency > threshold or errors spike we automatically route to stable-backup model in a different cluster.

[00:05:43] Evan: yes, the runtime supports policy-based routing today, but we need to validate compatibility across Dedicated and Private variants — sometimes fallback models aren't available in private infra.

[00:06:03] Sofia: that's critical — private end customers expect fallback too, but we may need to fallback to lower-capacity nodes in same VPC. document that as an explicit limitation.

[00:06:20] Priya: note to self: update the rollout playbook with a 'private deploy fallback limitations' section.

[00:06:29] Speaker 1: (mumbled) also, add a step for SSO/SCIM smoke for the enterprise flows, last time that sidecar dropped tokens.

[00:06:45] Ana: good call. I'll add SSO/SCIM smoke tests to the checklist.

[00:06:52] Marcus: another perf nuance — warmup is highly sensitive to batch size distribution. we should capture a histogram of request sizes and simulate the real mix during soak. otherwise the p99 numbers will lie.

[00:07:09] Evan: we can wire the trace logs to the dashboard and compare synthetic vs real histograms. i'll add that to the harness.

[00:07:20] Priya: about canary ramp — Daniel suggested 1%->5%->20% over six hours. do we want an intermediate 10% hold for 30 minutes?

[00:07:29] Daniel: yes, i prefer 1% (30m) -> 5% (60m) -> 10% (30m) -> 20% (rest). each step requires green on p50/p95/p99, errors, and cost telemetry.

[00:07:44] Sofia: and we should have an automatic rollback window where if any metric breaches the SLO it snaps back and gates require manual approval.

[00:07:54] Priya: agreed. capture that in the playbook.

[00:08:00] Evan: putting numbers on regression tolerance again: quality auto metric drop >2.5% OR human fail rate >3% triggers hold. cost increase >15% requires a PM sign-off.

[00:08:16] Marcus: add a operational failure mode for regional egress tax — if egress overage occurs in EU then we should pause the rollout in that region until we've remediated routing.

[00:08:29] Priya: ok, let's talk data retention and audit logs during the canary. legal asked for 90-day retention for audit trails and full request/response redaction for PII. how do we keep that without exploding storage?

[00:08:45] Sofia: we can sample full payloads at 1% and store metadata for 100%. attach a short doc — i will add recommended retention configs. also KMS rotation steps need to be included.

[00:08:59] Daniel: on the dry-run, let's include the sales and support on the invite so they can validate their alerting and docs.

[00:09:08] Ana: QA question — how many regression prompts should be in the smoke set? i propose 500 quick checks plus 50 human-review items.

[00:09:18] Priya: sounds right. Ana, you own the smoke set then.

[00:09:22] Ana: yep. will push to /s/qa/canary-smoke by monday.

[00:09:28] Evan: another item — quantization sometimes causes tokenization artifacts on structured outputs. we need a structural check (json-schema validation) as part of the automated checks.

[00:09:40] Marcus: good call, add schema validation to the pipeline.

[00:09:46] Speaker 2: (interrupt) also, something we missed last pilot: permission model regression where API keys scoped to older roles couldn't access new endpoints. make sure role migration test is in smoke.

[00:10:01] Sofia: i'll add role migration and KMS permission checks.

[00:10:07] Priya: timeline recap: we want bakeoff results by 5/26, soak finishing by 5/28, dry-run and release rehearsal by 5/23? that seems out of order — can we align dates?

[00:10:19] Daniel: dry-run needs to be after initial bakeoff and before 72h soak finish; propose dry-run 5/23, bakeoff 5/24-25, soak 5/25-27, final sign-off 5/28.

[00:10:33] Priya: ok, will consolidate schedule and send updated calendar invites.

[00:10:39] Evan: instrumentation — we need the dashboard to show 'delta cost per 1k tokens' and 'quality delta' side-by-side. otherwise it's hard to trade-off.

[00:10:50] Marcus: ops will publish a one-pager with threshold rules and automatic actions.

[00:10:56] Ana: QA will prepare the pass/fail criteria matrix and attach evidence links for each criteria.

[00:11:04] Priya: last items — are there any blockers?

[00:11:08] Sofia: we need the EU nat routing fix to be scheduled — i've put a ticket in infra backlog but need the exec ok to prioritize.

[00:11:16] Priya: i'll escalate.

[00:11:20] Marcus: we also need small changes to the runtime to expose a metric for 'kv cache hit after warmup' — Evan, can you prioritize a quick metric?

[00:11:29] Evan: yeah i'll add a Prometheus counter and surface it on the canary dashboard within 48 hours.

[00:11:36] Priya: great. recap of owners: Marcus - soak, Evan - harness & metrics, Ana - smoke tests, Sofia - infra validation, Daniel - dry-run. Priya will update playbook and schedule.

[00:11:51] Marcus: one more micro-note: during soak, let's run chaos monkey small-scale (one AZ) to ensure graceful degradation not global collapse.

[00:11:59] Daniel: agreed. include that in the soak plan.

[00:12:05] Priya: thanks everyone. i'll circulate the updated playbook and the calendar. meeting adjourned.

End transcript.
